newsitem.title: UK: IBCA gives Bank Leumi l-term A minus credit rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA gives Bank Leumi l-term A minus credit rating.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Monday it assigned its first credit rating of Bank Leumi (Leumi), Israel's second largest bank.

"Leumi, which is state-owned but scheduled for privatisation, has been assigned a long-term rating of A minus, a short-term rating of A2, an individual rating of B/C, and a legal rating of 2," IBCA said in a statement.
IBCA said by international standards the bank's profitability and capitalisation ratios, all of which are corrected for inflation, are respectable.
"Until 1995 Leumi had been struggling somewhat but it then managed something of a recovery, and its 1996 results were good," it said.

By dint of considerable provisioning, the most immediately alarming aspect of its risk profile, its exposure to the now financially defunct collectivised agricultural sector, has ceased to be a threat.
IBCA said most indications are that the bank's asset quality is improving and its prospects for 1997 look good.
"Recent belated progress in the peace process augurs better for the Israeli economy and for Leumi," the agency said.
